name: Tapeinosis

phase_0.boundary_condition: The rhetorical frame of the speech act which limits the scope of self-deprecation to the speaker's persona.

VINIT.justification: The state before the speaker assumes a persona or utters a claim.

TANCH.justification: The closure of the speech act that seals the intended effect on the audience.

AFWD.justification: The forward movement of establishing a baseline identity to be lowered.

AREV.justification: The downward morphism that reduces the perceived magnitude of the subject.

CLINK.justification: The chaining of modifiers that qualify and diminish the primary noun.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-referential identity that remains the subject of the reduction.

FSPLIT.justification: The division of the speaker's character into public reputation and private unworthiness.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the speaker as a unified but humbled entity.

EVALT.justification: The successful affirmative outcome where the audience accepts the speaker's humility.

EVALF.justification: The failure state where the reduction is viewed as false modesty or irony.

ENGAGR.justification: The state where the speaker is simultaneously high in status and low in expression.

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of the speech into a transcript or text.

phase_3.void_description: The absence of any rhetorical claim or social presence.
phase_3.true_description: The successful establishment of a humble ethos.
phase_3.false_description: The rejection of the speaker's persona as deceptive or arrogant.
phase_3.both_description: The paradoxical state of the 'great man' speaking as a 'lowly servant'.

steps.domain_action: The speaker stands before the audience in silence before beginning the exordium.
The speaker identifies themselves as the subject of the forthcoming discourse.
The speaker acknowledges their current social or professional standing to establish a baseline.
The speaker divides their persona into their external achievements and their internal limitations.
The speaker descends into the F-arm by enumerating personal flaws and lack of skill.
The speaker risks the audience perceiving this as a total failure of competence.
The speaker ascends the T-arm by attributing all success to external factors or the audience.
The speaker secures the affirmative branch of audience sympathy and rapport.
The speaker reunites the two branches into a single integrated persona of the humble expert.
The speaker chains this humble persona to the main argument of the speech.
The speaker maintains the tension of being an authority who claims no authority.
The specific phrasing of the tapeinosis is recorded in the minds of the listeners and the transcript.
The speech act concludes and the rhetorical boundary is sealed.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The cultural and linguistic norms governing modesty and social hierarchy.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The transmission of verbal and non-verbal cues between speaker and audience.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The collective memory of the audience regarding the speaker's past actions.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The rhythmic pacing of the speech which dictates when to lower the tone.
phase_5.alfs_store: Classical rhetorical manuals and historical examples of effective humility.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Social capital and the effort of linguistic precision.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A speaker with high perceived status and potential audience distance.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A speaker with maintained status but reduced audience friction.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The reduction in perceived ego is balanced by the increase in social cohesion.
